column1: # Night-Reed TG01/TG02 written lines (dialogue-write, one writer per speaker; text-reviewed). KEY<TAB>line; read by tools/ArgoniaPlugin/NightReed.cs.

column2: You opened the trapdoor with your own hand. Then you are a Lookout of the Night-Reed Chapter. Stay. I have work for you.
I have heard the dock thief is dead. You are a Lookout of the Night-Reed Chapter all the same, because you opened the trapdoor with your own hand. Stay. I have work for you.

A merchant's stilt house fell into the deep water just north of here, by the trapdoor. His lockbox is locked on the floor beside it. Ripper eels hunt that water. Three of his clients wait on the south bank. Bring the things in the box up before they find a diver. Do what you think best with them.
The beads are old family work. My family made them. They are worth nothing to a buyer.
All three are here. I will take them. Here are eighty gold.
Yes, it is Kothringi glass. I will not say otherwise. Here are fifty gold for the beads.
Take it. I could not sell it anyway. I want no trouble, so go.
Sixty gold. I had a buyer for this, you know. Here, it is yours.
The bone figurine is mine. It was carved for my clutch. It should come back to me.
You have the figurine, the charm and the beads. Good. Here is eighty gold. Take it.
Yes, it is worn smooth. It is older than my clutch. I will pay you fifty gold for it.
Very well. The Neesak charm was only pledged. I never sold it.
That is enough. The Neesak charm was only pledged. I never sold it.
All three. Good. Here are eighty gold.
You are right. A new silver mount means the merchant bought it outright. I will give you fifty gold for the charm.
Quiet work? This one does not sell it, but Khajiit knows who does. Go into the house on the dock behind this Khajiit and ask for Tilts-The-Jug. She sometimes has use for careful hands.

You ask plainly, so I will answer. Keeps-What-Floats drinks with me at the bench by the water until the lamps are low. Then he sleeps on a bedroll under the eaves of the shacks, north-west of the house. He runs from any shout, so keep your voice down.

That is a good drink, thank you. Keeps-What-Floats sits with me at the bench by the water until the lamps are low. Then he sleeps on a bedroll under the eaves of the shacks, north-west of the house. Shout at him and he runs.

The Chapter wants to see how you work. Keeps-What-Floats took a necklace of blue jaspers from another thief who was asleep. Bring it back and do not harm him. He carries the necklace on his round of the dock, so follow him. Sits-By-The-Water drinks with him.

He lives. You have good hands. Here are one hundred gold and three lockpicks. The Chapter's way down is a locked trapdoor at the edge of the deep water north of Pusbottom in Lilmoth. Take the coast ship from this dock. Open the trapdoor with your own hand, and speak to whoever waits below.

He is dead. The Chapter wanted the necklace and no killing, so there is no pay. Take three lockpicks all the same. The way down is a locked trapdoor at the edge of the deep water north of Pusbottom in Lilmoth. Take the coast ship from this dock. Open the trapdoor with your own hand, and speak to whoever waits below.
